title: Work graph (machine-checkable extract)
description: JSON sidecar for GRAPH.md and the AUTHORITATIVE DAG. Units + dependency edges + wave ordering + the enumerated tag vocabulary V_tag. Edge {from,to} means 'to consumes from'. The validator treats this graph.json as authoritative (fail-closed): if GRAPH.md exists it MUST be present, and cycles are detected on the union of `edges` and edges derived from each unit's `deps`. V_tag = the `v_tag` registry; every unit tag (and every brief tag) MUST be a member (enforced by validate_run.py, since JSON Schema cannot constrain one property's items to another data-provided array).

v_tag.description: The enumerated tag vocabulary V_tag for this run. Functions as the enum for every unit/brief `tags` value; membership is enforced mechanically by validate_run.py.

tags.description: This unit's tags, each a member of v_tag (V_tag). Basis for tag-scoped learnings propagation.

dod_refs.description: OPTIONAL (guardrail enforcement). The clarifications.json definition_of_done items this unit serves — each element VERBATIM ∈ definition_of_done. A bound unit serves ≥ 1 DoD item (minItems 1). Deliberately NOT in `required`: requiredness is the validator's adoption-closure (I20 — once ANY unit carries dod_refs, EVERY unit must, with a brief.json mirror), keeping archived runs schema-valid.

non_goal_refs.description: OPTIONAL (guardrail enforcement). The clarifications.json non_goals items this unit must actively respect — each element VERBATIM ∈ non_goals. MAY be [] (an explicit, distinguishable 'no non-goal applies to this unit' statement — no minItems; empty-STRING elements still barred), while an ABSENT key under adoption is an I21 closure FAIL. Same adoption-closure + brief-mirror posture as dod_refs.

deliverable.description: I54 (1.14.0, Drift fix 2) — the shipping-versus-finding distinction, and the ONLY definition of it: this key is PLANNER-WRITTEN and lives HERE, on graph.json, never in debrief.json. That is the whole point of the field — the counter is then computable BEFORE the units run and WITHOUT trusting the agent being counted; an executor-written variant would be a self-report by exactly the party the clock measures. 'ships' means the unit's outputs[] include at least one path OUTSIDE the run directory — a change to the thing the human asked about. 'informs' means it produces a finding, a measurement, a document section or a decision input, and nothing the human asked for changes when it lands. OPTIONAL in the schema (absent => unclassified), so no archived graph becomes invalid; made effectively mandatory by the adoption-gated I54-1 rather than by `required`. I56 (the consecutive-non-shipping cap) CONSUMES this field READ-ONLY and never widens the enum. HONEST BOUNDARY: this is DECLARED shipping intent, not shipped reality — a unit can carry 'ships' and ship nothing, and no shipped predicate checks the label's correctness.

priority_class.description: I53 (1.14.0, Drift fix 1) — whether this unit exists because a human ASKED for it or because the run generated it for itself. Absent => 'normal'. DERIVED, NEVER ASSERTED: a unit may carry 'directive' only if it appears in the units_added of an amendment whose origin.trigger == 'human_request' and whose origin.directive_ref RESOLVES to a directives/H<NN>.json on disk (I53-3). OPTIONAL, so this is a widening; making it `required` later would be a REVISES of the graph contract and should not be done. HONEST BOUNDARY: making a self-declared enum readable does not make it true — genuineness stays OBSERVABLE (Limitation AD), because no predicate over a run directory can tell a true quotation of the maintainer from a fabricated one.

frame.description: OPTIONAL (1.15.0 blast radius). The unit's declared write scope, frozen at Phase 4 and mirrored verbatim into the unit's brief.json `frame`. `modifies[]` holds the repository path patterns (relative to the workspace root) the unit may create, edit or delete — a captured change that no unit's `modifies` matches is recorded as unattributed; `immutable[]` holds patterns the unit must never touch; `intended_changes[]` states, in prose, the behaviour changes the unit is expected to cause (what a differential or a broken consumer can be reconciled against); `modifies_none_reason` explains a deliberately empty `modifies` (a unit that changes no repository path). Deliberately NOT in the unit's `required`: whether a run of a given stamp must carry it is decided by the version-gated validator predicates, keeping archived graphs schema-valid. Inside, only the three lists are required so a present frame is always well-formed; the explicit-none rule for an empty `modifies` is the validator's to enforce. Carries no key that switches a blast check off.

revision.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). The graph revision number: 1 at Phase-4 approval (T6), incremented by exactly 1 per applied amendment record. Absent => revision 1 (no amendments). Cross-checked by validate_run.py I18: revision == 1 + |amendment records|.

amendments_applied.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). The amendment ids (A<NN>) applied to this graph, in order. I18 requires it to list exactly the amendments/A<NN>.json record ids in order; uniqueItems (WP3) forbids a duplicated id.

baseline_units.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). The revision-1 (T6) unit-id set: exactly units[] at Phase-4 approval, written ONCE and IMMUTABLE thereafter. REQUIRED once revision > 1 (schema allOf below). validate_run.py I17 reconciles set(units[]) ∪ set(retired) == set(baseline_units) ∪ ⋃ amendment units_added, so a smuggled or phantom-added/retired unit is caught. Absent => revision 1 (no amendments).

fuel_initial.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). The fuel seed written ONCE at Phase-4 approval (T6) and IMMUTABLE. Anchors the mutable fsm-state.expansion.fuel_initial: validate_run.py I18 (WP2) requires expansion.fuel_initial == graph.fuel_initial, so widening fuel mid-run (B4) is tamper-evident. REQUIRED once revision > 1 (schema allOf below).

retired_units.description: OPTIONAL (Bounded Graph Amendments). Units retired by a split_unit/cancel_unit amendment: {id, replaced_by[], amendment}. A retired id never reappears in units[] and (I17) never carries a debrief/verify.

socratic.description: OPTIONAL. The planner/architect's canonical 4-key socratic block (result of the FORK.COUNTER.ADMIT.PIVOT.RESIDUAL self-interrogation over the decomposition's load-bearing claim), same shape as debrief/verify. When present, validate_run.py's I13 check requires `counter` to record an OUTCOME (rejects blank/'n/a'). This is the schema-enforced landing place for the planner's socratic residue (D-07): the planner produces no debrief.json, so the block lives here.

allOf.$comment: BGA (WP1/WP2): once the graph has been amended (revision > 1), both the immutable revision-1 baseline_units set (I17 reconciliation) and the immutable fuel_initial seed (I18 fuel anchor) MUST be present. revision 1 (or absent) => neither required.
